The reports do not establish uninterrupted closure for every commodity, normal private trading or a precise original shutdown date.

verification.notes: Last-arrival versus halt-onset conflict retained; one wood consignment and later small reverse flows only.

summary: Normal opening arrangements at Singkhon–Mawtaung on the Thailand–Myanmar border were constrained in 2026 by fighting and difficulty coordinating with an authorised Myanmar counterpart. A limited goods-transfer schedule was eased from twice-weekly morning sessions to daily daytime permission from 17 April, while advance notification and customs conditions remained. Later discussions about general reopening do not establish that all passenger and trade services had resumed.

verification.notes: Formal opening obstacle separated from narrower goods permission and later plans.

summary: Cameroon ordered its borders closed ahead of legislative and municipal elections on 9 February 2020, with the announced window running from 7 February until reopening the day after polling. International flights were expressly exempt. The order concerned election security, but available reports do not identify the treatment of individual land crossings or confirm their actual first resumed passage on 10 February.

verification.notes: National land order and air exemption; scheduled endpoint not observed operation.

summary: Cameroon announced closure of its land borders from 10 October 2025 ahead of the 12 October presidential election, with reopening scheduled for 13 October. The territorial administration ministry presented the measure as part of election-security arrangements. Reports establish the planned national restriction but do not document individual checkpoint enforcement, land-travel exceptions or the first actual crossings after it ended.

verification.notes: Corroborated 48-hour-before-election schedule; no domestic exemptions transferred.

summary: The Republic of Congo ordered national borders closed from 06:00 to 18:00 on 10 July 2022 for local elections and the first round of legislative voting. The order included land-border movement but did not list individual checkpoints or exceptions. This was a twelve-hour announced restriction; actual enforcement and reopening were not observed, and separate domestic travel rules did not define its border exceptions.

verification.notes: Twelve-hour first-round order only; domestic circulation exemptions excluded.

summary: Cameroon restricted movement along its Equatorial Guinea frontier during the February 2023 fever outbreak, citing the risk of importing disease. Merchants were still reporting difficulties in March, while health and police teams were instructed to facilitate goods movements. The available reports do not establish an all-goods ban, precise restrictions at each post or a reopening date; the later declaration that the outbreak had ended was not itself a repeal of border controls.

verification.notes: Disease-control travel restrictions separated from facilitated goods and epidemiological end.

summary: Coal exports through Shiveekhuren–Ceke on the Mongolia–China border were interrupted during a COVID-19 outbreak in late 2021, with one mining company reporting exports suspended from November until May. Limited trial coal-truck movement resumed on 25 May 2022. Accounts differ over the initial port closure date, and the return did not establish normal capacity, passenger access or the same uninterrupted restriction for every exporter.

verification.notes: Company suspension and port-onset conflict distinguished; limited coal trial endpoint.

summary: Coal movements through Gashuunsukhait–Ganqimaodu on the Mongolia–China border were interrupted in August 2021 amid COVID-19 testing requirements. Reports described coal transport returning on either 30 or 31 August after more than a week of disruption, while copper-powder trucks had crossed during the interruption. The evidence does not establish one exact start or a universal customs closure, and testing delays continued after coal movements resumed.

verification.notes: Coal versus copper traffic; disputed reopening day and no universal authority halt.

summary: Mongolia arranged a COVID-19 freight closure at Tsagaannuur–Tashanta on the Russian border from 2 to 23 November 2020. Petroleum trucks were then admitted under limited periodic arrangements, with fuel arrivals reported on 23 November and empty trucks returning the same day. Later fodder and wider-goods permissions had their own schedules, so the fuel movement did not establish unrestricted daily freight reopening or passenger access.

verification.notes: Scheduled closure and petroleum-only exception; later goods permissions distinct.

summary: Namibia prohibited imports of susceptible animals, raw animal products and potentially infectious feed or materials from Botswana from 25 August 2022 following a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak. Sealed transit of goods from third countries through Botswana remained permitted under conditions. The restriction was still reported on 31 August, but the available evidence does not establish its lifting date or the exact implementation at each border post.

verification.notes: Botswana-origin animal-health restriction with sealed third-country transit exception.

summary: Botswana announced an immediate ban on cloven-hoofed livestock and related products from Zimbabwe on 19 January 2026 because of foot-and-mouth disease risk. The restriction concerned those animals and products entering Botswana, rather than travellers or all imports. Later easing of Botswana’s internal livestock movements does not establish repeal of this Zimbabwe-origin import ban, whose complete duration and border-level enforcement remain unverified.

verification.notes: Foreign import ban separated from domestic disease-zone exceptions and easing.

summary: Botswana restricted imports and transit of South African cloven-hoofed livestock and animal products on 9 or 10 January 2019 after a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak. On 30 January, it permitted selected products and animals from unaffected provinces under conditions, while live animals from affected Limpopo areas remained excluded. This was a partial policy easing, not unrestricted reopening for every animal product or a general passenger restriction.

verification.notes: Onset disagreement and partial product/province-specific relaxation retained.

summary: A logistics advisory reported cross-border trucking suspended at Alashankou on the China–Kazakhstan border in August 2021, while rail services were congested rather than stopped. A later Xinjiang transport report listed Alashankou among road ports retaining freight clearance by 29 October. The reports do not establish the precise start, official road-specific reason or first resumed truck, so they cannot support a continuous closure between those observations.

verification.notes: Road suspension not railway closure; indexed later freight access and unknown reason retained.
